title: Privilege binding model and permission schema for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goals: define a production-ready RBAC v2 privilege binding model that supports resource-scoped role bindings, tenant and project isolation, SAML group -> role-set mapping, and tight audit log correlation. Deliverables: canonical resource hierarchy, scope semantics, permission matrix (CRUD + operational scopes), role-set vs binding semantics, migration mapping from RBAC v1, and admin emergency controls (break-glass, impersonation audit). Must handle multi-tenant isolation, Dedicated/Private deployment variants, and be performant at token-evaluation scale.

permission_matrix_summary: Permission axes: read, write, deploy, manage (role/setting changes), audit_view (view audit trails), impersonate (run-as), approve_deploy, configure_billing. Each resource type has a minimal default role-set mapping and an explicit deny list supported via deny-bindings at tenant-level. Role-sets are composable; bindings attach a role-set to a principal at a specific scope (resource path). Effective permission resolution applies precedence: explicit deny > explicit allow at exact scope > allow inherited from parent scope > default deny.
resource_hierarchy: Canonical path pattern: /global | /tenant/{tenant_id} | /tenant/{tenant_id}/org/{org_id} | /tenant/{tenant_id}/org/{org_id}/project/{project_id} | /.../environment/{env} | /.../model/{model_id} | /.../route/{route_id}. Bindings may be attached at any node; evaluation uses longest-prefix match plus deny overrides.
sso_saml_notes: SAML mapping: support groupAttribute + customNameId formats. Implementation must namespace group identifiers with IdP issuer to avoid collisions. Suggested default flow: on assertion, map groups -> role-sets via configurable mapping table; also support attribute-based temporary role elevations (timeboxed) for contractors. All SSO mappings should emit events to audit log with correlation_id for traceability.
audit_logging_considerations: Every permission-evaluation and binding mutation must emit structured audit events: {actor, principal, action, resource_path, evaluated_permissions, result, reason, correlation_id, timestamp}. Events are append-only and indexed by correlation_id and resource_path for efficient query. Sensitive fields (tokens) must be redacted; KMS-backed signing of critical events planned for Dedicated/private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Security team and Platform PM
Schema migrations validated on staging with backward-compatibility tests to RBAC v1 mapping
Permission evaluation implementation passes unit + integration tests and keeps median auth latency increase <= 2ms and p99 <= 8ms in staging
SAML group -> role-set mapping end-to-end tested against Okta and Azure AD test IdPs
Audit events emitted for binding changes and permission evaluations and searchable in Console trace for a sample tenant
Feature gated behind 'rbac_v2' flag with CLI toggle for emergency rollback
testing_plan: Unit tests for permission resolution precedence and deny overrides
Integration tests with database migration (copyback strategy) and feature-flag toggles
E2E SAML tests using Okta + Azure AD sandbox accounts; verify group mapping and attribute-based elevations
Load test: simulate 5k auth checks/s for permission cache warming and measure latency/CPU impact
Audit log verification: replay events to Elastic/Lake and validate retention/field redaction
migration_and_rollback: Migration approach: phased rollout. 1) Add role_sets + bindings tables alongside v1 schema and populate mappings using deterministic map script. 2) Populate effective_permissions cache for active tenants lazily on first auth. 3) Gradually switch evaluation path behind 'rbac_v2' flag per-tenant. Rollback: re-enable v1 evaluation path and remove v2 eval; DB writes are idempotent — binding writes are recorded to audit log to support manual reconciliation. Have a fallback path that, on catastrophic failures, treats bindings as read-only and falls back to conservative deny-all for non-admin routes.
